feature: A copy is not asked to decide what its original decides
summary: The Layout section on a copy of a component now reads out how it arranges its contents instead of offering fields for it, and says to change it on the original. Before this, padding or a gap typed into a copy was accepted and then thrown away by the next edit anywhere in the document.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Needs the Components, Placement and Auto Layout flags, which are on by default.

try.do: Draw two rectangles, select both, and press Layer > Stack Selection.
Type 16 into Padding in the Layout section.
Open the Library, switch it to Comps, and drag the new tile onto empty canvas.
Read the Layout section of the copy that lands selected.
Press Edit Original in the Component section, then type 32 into Padding.
Click the copy again and read its Layout section: it says 32.

evaluate: When you pick the copy, is it obvious within a second that Layout is being reported to you rather than asked of you?
Does the last line of the section tell you where to go, or do you still hunt for the original?
Is the arrangement in a sentence better than the same numbers in fields you cannot type in?
Do you ever want a single copy to have its OWN padding, or is a copy that always matches its original what you expect?
On the original, does the Layout section feel unchanged?
rough: There is no way to give one copy its own padding. Refusing is honest, but if you want per copy overrides that is a separate feature and I did not build it.

The copy's sentence keeps the app's existing phrasing, so a column stack reads 'lines up down', which is a little awkward. It matches what the original's own caption says, so I left both alone rather than changing one of them.
The section header still reads 'Contents of <copy name>', though the contents are the original's. Naming the selected thing seemed better than naming a layer that is somewhere else on the canvas.
Screenshots are real window captures from Scripts/playtest/copy-layout-walk.json, taken with the probe's Screen Recording grant.
